causes.lines: 33-52 (check 'release CLI runs its in-process gate from spaced and percent-looking checkout paths'; setup at 35, 46, 47; failing assert at 49)
causes.cause: The test finds git with `which git` (35), symlinks it into a private folder under the extensionless name 'git' (46), and runs the release CLI with PATH set to that folder alone (47). On Windows, libuv's PATH search for a bare command name tries only 'git.com' and 'git.exe', never an extensionless 'git'. So spawnSync('git') in scripts/template-release.mjs:15 fails with ENOENT. runRelease then stops at :31-32 with 'release failed: cannot resolve commit (spawnSync git ENOENT)', before it ever reaches the default acceptance gate that would name uvx. The log prints that exact message, so the ENOENT and the early stop are confirmed. Two compounding points are inferred, not seen in the log: (a) `which` here is Git for Windows' MSYS which.exe, which prints a POSIX path such as /mingw64/bin/git, so the link would dangle even under the name git.exe; (b) a symlinked Git launcher may also fail to find its install or DLLs. Node passes PATH (not Path) to the child, because 'PATH' sorts before 'Path' in its case-insensitive dedupe, which fits the ENOENT. The check at 48 passed because status was 1, and line 35 did not throw. The other four checks inject runGit and gate and pass on Windows. The product behaves correctly on Windows with a normal PATH, because git.exe is found there. The release job runs only on ubuntu-latest (ci.yml:75-100).
causes.fix: Test-only. On win32, resolve git with `execFileSync('where', ['git'])`, take the first line, trim it, and set PATH to path.dirname of that path (Git\cmd, which holds git.exe and no uvx). Do not symlink there. Keep the POSIX `which` plus symlink path unchanged. Put that one helper in a shared test helper and use it in template-acceptance.test.mjs:49-62 too. That file has the identical pattern and fails in the same run with 'template acceptance failed: git could not start'. A declared win32 skip is a fallback, since releases run only on ubuntu. It would leave R-596's CLI path unpinned on Windows, so the directory-on-PATH fix is preferred.

causes.cause: The g-signal fixture calls process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGKILL'). On win32, libuv turns that into TerminateProcess(handle, 1), so the runner's child 'exit' event sees code 1 and signal null. scripts/test.mjs:405 then prints 'exit 1' rather than 'exit SIGKILL', and the /exit SIG/ clause fails. The FAIL label clause should still hold. The runner behaves correctly: no Windows API lets a parent see a signal for a child that kills itself.
causes.fix: Make the predicate depend on the platform. On POSIX keep labelFor === 'FAIL' && /exit SIG/. On win32 assert labelFor === 'FAIL' && /— exit 1$/ on the g-signal line, because a Windows self-kill has no signal to name. Optionally note in the check name that the signal is named on POSIX only. Leave scripts/test.mjs alone.

causes.cause: The CLI child never gets past its first git call, so it never reaches uvx. Log, confirmed: assertion input is 'template acceptance failed: git could not start'. That text comes from scripts/template-acceptance.mjs:75 only when the git spawn returns no output at all, i.e. a spawn error, not a git error (a failing rev-parse would print 'fatal: ...'). The same log shows the identical shim pattern in template-release.test.mjs failing with 'spawnSync git ENOENT'. Why git cannot spawn (inferred, not visible in the log): line 51 runs MSYS `which git` under the CI bash shell, which prints a POSIX path such as /mingw64/bin/git; line 57 links that as an extensionless 'git'; libuv's Windows PATH search only tries name+.com and name+.exe for an extensionless command, so toolBin/git is never found (and its target is also an MSYS path, so the link dangles). Only the first loop iteration ('acceptance path with spaces') ran; the 'a%20b' iteration never ran. The product's main guard did work on Windows (the CLI reached runAcceptance from a RUNNER~1 temp path with spaces).
causes.fix: On win32, find the real git with `execFileSync("where", ["git"], {encoding:"utf8"}).split(/\r?\n/)[0].trim()` and set the child PATH to path.dirname(thatGitExe) instead of building toolBin with a symlink (keep the which+symlink path on POSIX, or use the dirname approach everywhere). Do NOT link git.exe into toolBin: Git for Windows' launcher finds its install root from its own location, so a linked or copied git.exe may still fail (inferred). The git folder holds no uvx, so the 'reports missing uvx' assertion still exercises the product. Best as one shared test helper also used by template-release.test.mjs:35 and immutable-review.test.mjs:199, which use the same `which git` pattern.
